pr_title: feat: add calendar cache status and actions (#22532)

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] UI may show stale cache timestamp after delete

After `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` succeeds, the component only shows a toast and calls `onSuccess`, but it does not invalidate `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. If the parent `onSuccess` doesn't refetch, `cacheUpdatedAt` can remain displayed even though the cache rows were deleted; invalidate/refetch the connectedCalendars query on success/settled to keep the UI consistent.
validations.impact: After deleting calendar cache, the UI continues to display the old cacheUpdatedAt timestamp because the connectedCalendars query is never invalidated, misleading users into thinking the cache still exists.
validations.reasoning: The deleteCacheMutation (lines 44-51) only calls showToast and onSuccess?.() on success. It does NOT call utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate(). Compare with disconnectMutation (lines 53-63) which properly invalidates in onSettled. The parent passes onChanged as onSuccess, but onChanged is typed as optional (onChanged?: () => unknown | Promise<unknown>) and there is no guarantee it invalidates the connectedCalendars query. The cacheUpdatedAt prop will retain its stale value until a manual page refresh.

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] macOS-specific sed -i syntax will fail on Linux

The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...`, which is BSD/macOS syntax. On Linux (GNU sed), this will error and the env var won't be updated; use a portable approach (e.g. `sed -i.bak ... && rm -f ...` or branch on OS) so the script works in CI/dev environments that run Linux.
validations.impact: The script will fail to update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in .env on Linux systems, causing the webhook test setup to silently break in CI or on Linux dev machines.
validations.reasoning: Line 67 uses `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|" "$ENV_FILE"` which is BSD/macOS sed syntax. On GNU/Linux sed, the empty string '' after -i is treated as the next argument (the regex), not a backup suffix. GNU sed interprets -i'' (no space) differently from -i '' (with space). This would cause an error or incorrect behavior on Linux. The script has no OS detection or portable fallback.
